topIssues.title: op-challenger: make the ZK actor challenge proposals not derivable at l1Head, as fault-proof games do
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The ZK dispute game actor accepts a proposal whose root matches the canonical super root, even when the root can't be derived from L1 data available at the game's `l1Head`. The fault-proof challenger disputes such proposals in both output-root and super-root games. The ZK actor should follow the same rule.

This is a consistency fix, not a safety bug. A proposal like this has a correct root, so if nobody challenges it, a correct root is accepted. Honest proposers don't create these proposals; the only case is an L1 reorg that pushes the batch past `l1Head` after the proposer has read its node.

## Current behaviour

ZK actor (`op-challenger/game/zk/actor.go:156-166`, `isValidProposal`):

1. It requires `resp.CurrentL1 > l1Head`.
2. It treats `resp.Data == nil` as invalid.
3. Otherwise it returns `resp.Data.SuperRoot == proposalHash`.

It never compares `resp.Data.VerifiedRequiredL1` with `l1Head`.

Fault-proof challenger:

- **Super-root games** (`op-challenger/game/fault/trace/super/provider.go:86-87`): `VerifiedRequiredL1 > l1Head` gives `InvalidTransition`, so the proposal is disputed.
- **Output-root games** (`op-challenger/game/fault/trace/outputs/provider.go:71-88`): the honest trace is clamped to the safe head at `l1Head`, so a proposal beyond it is disputed.

## Why match the fault-proof rule

- **It's the rule the proof enforces.** `ZKDisputeGame.prove` verifies against `abi.encode(l1Head(), startingProposal.root, rootClaim(), l2SequenceNumber(), msg.sender)` (`packages/contracts-bedrock/src/dispute/zk/ZKDisputeGame.sol:533-534`). If such a proposal is challenged, nobody can prove it, so the challenger wins.
- **The verdict shouldn't depend on node sync.** Today it does: if the source node's response omits `Data`, the actor calls the proposal invalid; otherwise it compares hashes. Two honest challengers can reach different verdicts on the same proposal.
- **Validity should mean the same thing across game types.**

## Proposed fix

In `isValidProposal`, treat `resp.Data.VerifiedRequiredL1.Number > l1Head.Number` as invalid. Add a unit test where the proposal matches the canonical root but its `VerifiedRequiredL1` is above `l1Head`, and assert that the actor challenges it.

topIssues.title: interop: expire and refund undelivered cross-chain sends (bridge cancels)
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Problem

If an interop message is never relayed on the destination chain, the sender's funds are stuck. For example, a `SuperchainETHBridge` send whose relay can't execute on the destination has no way back to the sender.

## Design

- Interop messages expire after a fixed window, capped at 7 days.
- `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` records when each message was sent.
- A new exporter predeploy proves "never relayed" back to the source chain through L1.
- The source chain then marks the message expired, and `SuperchainETHBridge` refunds expired sends.
- The expiry length is a constructor parameter so tests can shorten it. Guards make sure production networks use the right value.

## PRs (review in order)

1. #23276: cap the message expiry window at 7 days (Go, kona, interop filter)
2. #23277: acceptance tests and devstack DSL for message expiry
3. #23286: expire undelivered interop messages (contracts)
4. #23284: refund expired `SuperchainETHBridge` sends
5. #23278: docs

Formal verification work: #23263

## Remaining

- [ ] Review and merge the stack.
- [ ] Add an end-to-end acceptance test that fast-forwards L2 time by 7 days. This needs the time-travel clock in the op-node sequencer, and kona would need an RPC for it. The fallback is a shortened expiry set through the constructor.
- [ ] Add the contract changes to the Lagoon L2 audit scope.
- [ ] If this ships in Lagoon, include it in the re-snapshotted Lagoon NUT bundle (#23314).

topPRs.title: op-deployer,op-chain-ops!: run every deploy script on forge and delete the Go script host
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
This PR is split into a stack for review: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The stack has later review fixes; this PR stays open as the CI-green reference.

op-deployer ran its deploy scripts on `op-chain-ops/script`, an in-process Go EVM. That host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has (cheatcode precompiles, pranks, no code-size limit), so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). After this PR, forge is the only script engine, and the Go host and `op-chain-ops/interopgen` are deleted.

**Effect on users**

- op-deployer runs forge for every deployment, and anvil for `prepare` and `continue`. It downloads the pinned Foundry release on Linux and macOS when the tools are not on PATH. The Docker images ship both.
- Genesis deployments (`apply --deployment-target genesis`, op-e2e, sysgo) run the scripts offline on forge. The L1 and L2 genesis output does not change: before the switch, a differential test found equal state roots from both engines on eight reference intents.
- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` broadcast with forge, one transaction at a time, and no longer through op-service's txmgr. As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction. forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- `prepare` and `continue` simulate the deployment on an ephemeral anvil fork of the L1, as the deployer, without its key. `continue` then checks the simulated transactions and replays them to L1 through txmgr.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle that would make forge compile, or whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a bundle must come from the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without the FFI cheatcode, with file access only to the artifacts and to op-deployer's state directory, and forge scripts and anvil inherit only the environment variables that they need (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). anvil listens on loopback without CORS.
- forge runs need the `lib/` sources of the bundle but no solc compiler. Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- Removed: the `calldata` and `noop` deployment targets, `op-deployer manage`, the `--use-forge` and `--forge-slow-broadcast` flags, the Windows release binaries and `DeploymentCalldata` in `state.json`. contracts-bedrock loses the `InteropMigration` script and `DummyCaller`.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time. Without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- Bundle builds run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, as CI's `forge-build` already does. A single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build, and then forge compiles on the first run. The builds then check that a second run compiles nothing, and fail if it does.
- The interop harness and sysgo now run the interop migration on a live L1 through an EIP-7702 delegation from the ProxyAdmin owner, not in the genesis state. The L1 activates Prague at genesis for this.
- The test `RetryProxy` (op-service) now gives a client error (4xx, but not 429) to the client at once. forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the proxy held each of these calls for about 40 s of retries, so the Sepolia tests of `init` timed out.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass is done, and forge stops after a few quick retries.
- #23309 (genesis-output changes) is not in this PR, on purpose. It changes genesis output, which this PR must not do.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout (op-e2e, sysgo, kona proof tests) now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache, where the Go host read only artifact JSON.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. Online, it resolves them from its built-in list and runs the cached artifacts.
- The `forge` package tests (anvil fork, compile stop, sandbox, environment, slots) run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Review findings not fixed here**

- Live `apply`/`bootstrap` could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does. The #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast` for live deploys; this is a follow-up if fee bumping matters for these one-time deployments.
- The op-e2e interop harness and sysgo could share one `opcm.MigrateInput` type, and sysgo could check that its rollup configs and dependency set name the same chains, as interopgen did. Both are follow-ups.
- `opcm.NewForgeClient` takes no context for the forge download, and `opcm.PermissionedGameStartingAnchorRoot` now has only test users. Both are unchanged.
- Security review, not fixed: `continue` checks the sender, target, type and value of the call it replays, but not its calldata against the prepared input (that needs the script's encoding in Go); the RPC URL stays on the command line of forge and anvil, which have no environment binding for it; a crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe); and a forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23300, #23301, #23302, #23304, #23305, #23306, #23307 and #23308.

BREAKING CHANGE: The Go packages `op-chain-ops/script`, `op-chain-ops/interopgen`, `op-deployer/pkg/env`, `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage` and `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/upgrade` are removed. So are `opcm.Scripts`, the script-host `opcm` constructors, the `opcm.*ViaForge` functions (now `opcm.DeploySuperchain`, `opcm.DeployImplementations`, `opcm.DeployOPChain`, `opcm.DeployAltDA`, `opcm.DeployDisputeGame`, `opcm.DeployMIPS`, `opcm.DeployAlphabetVM`, `opcm.ReadImplementationAddresses` and `opcm.ReadSuperchainDeployment`, which take an `opcm.ForgeEnv`), `ApplyPipelineOpts.PrivateKey`, `UseForge` and `ReceiptQueryInterval`, and in `broadcaster` the `Broadcaster` interface, `CalldataBroadcaster`, `CaptureBroadcaster`, `NoopBroadcaster` and `BroadcastCreate2`. Go programs run Solidity scripts with forge, for example through op-deployer's `forge` package, take the upgrade input types from `opcm`, and build interop test worlds with an op-deployer intent. op-deployer users get forge and anvil from the release images, or let op-deployer download them. Users of `--use-forge`, `--forge-slow-broadcast`, or the `calldata` and `noop` targets drop them; forge is always used. Intents that point at an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier contracts release use `embedded` instead. To move chains to interop, call `OPContractsManagerV2.migrate` as a delegatecall from the chains' ProxyAdmin owner, for example from a superchain-ops task.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: add spn-wallet to fund and inspect SPN requesters
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
With op-signer, the op-zk-proposer SPN requester is a KMS key that can sign only SPN messages. It cannot deposit PROVE for itself, and operators have no tool to fund it. `spn-wallet` funds any SPN account from another signer, `PRIVATE_KEY` or a GCP Cloud KMS key, and the recipient signs nothing. It also reads balances, history, proof requests and bids without a key. The README's "Funding the SPN requester" section is the runbook.

Write commands preview by default and send only with `--broadcast`. `--max-fee` is then required, and `fund --from-l1` checks it before PROVE leaves L1. `fund` treats the transfer as done once the recipient's history shows the TRANSFER_IN for its hash. A balance check would be wrong here, because a requester pays for proofs while it waits and its balance can stay low after the credit.

Builds on wwared's `feat/spn-wallet` commit, which is kept as the first commit. Refs #21419; the alerting half of that issue is not part of this PR.

topPRs.title: op-deployer!: run live apply and bootstrap on forge by default
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stack 2/7, merge in order: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The whole change, with green CI, is #23647.

The Go script host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has, so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). op-deployer already had an opt-in forge path for live deployments. This PR makes that path dependable and the default for live `apply` and `bootstrap`. Genesis deployments, the L2 genesis, `prepare` and `continue` still run on the Go script host; later PRs of the stack move them.

**Effect on users**

- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` run on forge. `--use-forge=false` still runs them on the Go script host, until #23308 removes the flag. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed: every broadcast sends one transaction at a time.
- As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction.
- forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a live deployment needs the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works, and `--use-forge=false` keeps the Go script host until #23308.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without FFI, with file access only to the artifacts, and forge inherits only the environment variables that it needs (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- The artifacts-locators page no longer lists `tag://` locators, which op-deployer already rejects. The manual Sepolia test script no longer offers the Go script host as its default engine.
- The forge download detects musl, uses `--cache-dir`, and gives a clear error without network access. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time: without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. A compile watcher enforces "never compile" instead.
- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Bundle builds (Docker, melange, `just forge-build`) run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, and fail when a second run would compile: a single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys chains: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass, and forge gives up after a few quick retries.
- The test `RetryProxy` gives a client error (4xx, not 429) to the client at once: forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the retries held each call for about 40 s.
- The `forge` package tests run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Reviews**

go-code-reviewer on the transitional code of this PR and the next two. Fixed: the BREAKING CHANGE text named `tag://` instead of `https://`/`file://` bundles, and `--use-forge=false` had no test (a live subtest now covers it).

**Known limits, not fixed here**

Live deploys could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does (#23306); the #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast`. The RPC URL stays on the command line of forge, which has no environment binding for it. A crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe). A forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23302.

BREAKING CHANGE: `op-deployer apply` and `op-deployer bootstrap` run on forge by default; `--use-forge=false` runs them on the Go script host until a later release removes it. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed. An `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier contracts release is refused for live `apply` and `bootstrap`; use `embedded`, or `--use-forge=false` until the Go script host is removed. Go callers replace `ApplyPipelineOpts.UseForge`, `ForgeSlowBroadcast` and `PrivateKey` with `UseScriptHost` (zero value: forge) and `DeployerPrivateKey`; `pipeline.Env`'s `ForgeClient`, `UseForge`, `L1RPCUrl` and `PrivateKey` with `Forge`; and bootstrap's `UseForge` and `ForgeSlowBroadcast` with `UseScriptHost`. `forge.ScriptCaller` returns `(output, error)` without the recompiled flag, and `forge.Client.SlowBroadcast` is removed. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

topPRs.title: op-reth: settle SDM refunds during canonical RPC replay
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Related to ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485. Canonical transaction and block replays include SDM settlement, so debug gas, replayed balances/state diffs, and intermediate roots agree with execution. This is an independent line of work based on George’s #23615/#23616, with canonical versus diagnostic replay separated and the supplied transaction environment preserved.

Depends on ethereum-optimism/reth#26. The temporary PR-head pin must be replaced with the merged fork tag before merging this PR. Raw/bad-block tracing keeps its existing permissive, pre-refund behavior; parity call-frame gas keeps its existing convention.

Adds imported multi-transaction coverage, an unrefunded gap, refund-dependent affordability, modified-environment replay, direct OTS/call-many checks, and traceChain success/error alignment. CI op-reth integration tests pass: 81 passed and one skipped, including both multi-transaction settlement regressions. Nightly formatting passes. CI workspace tests, clippy, builds, documentation, and Rust merge gates pass on the latest push; two Go end-to-end memory jobs remain pending. The prerequisite’s helper unit tests and workspace all-features clippy pass. Mirror checker unit tests pass, while existing stale mirror entries still fail its repository-wide check.

Static Rust and pin/deposit reviews were performed. Full workspace, JS-tracer feature, and forward-upstream-release reviews have not been run; this pin adds only the prerequisite RPC commit to the existing fork release.

topPRs.title: kona-gossip,kona-disc!: Test peering in memory and fix the bugs it exposed
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
**What**
Part 1 of static peers (#23430): network tests can now run nodes on libp2p's in-memory transport and connect them explicitly. Getting the existing network tests to run discovery for real exposed several peering bugs, which this PR also fixes.

**Why**
Static peers need tests where peers connect only through configured addresses, and restart on the same address. The memory transport gives that, in milliseconds. While building it, we found these problems:
- Test nodes advertised UDP port 0, so discv5 never actually ran in any test. They passed only because bootnode ENRs get dialed directly. `Discv5Builder` now binds a free port for a listen port of 0 and advertises it. op-devstack starts kona-node with `--p2p.listen.udp 0`.
- The gater treated `peer_redialing: None` as "never redial", the opposite of its docs. So with `GaterConfig::default()`, as in tests, a node gave up on a peer after one failed dial. The CLI's default of 500 hid this.
- When two peers dial each other at once from their listen ports, TCP merges the dials into one connection and the Noise handshake fails. On macOS, redials then fail with `AddrInUse` for ~30s. Dials now use fresh ports. The resulting duplicate connection is closed after a 10s grace period, because gossipsub sends its subscriptions only on a peer's first connection.
- Discovery re-sending a connected peer's ENR reached the gater, which refused it as "already dialing".

Operators can now use `--p2p.listen.udp 0`, and an advertised port of 0 falls back to the listen port. After deploy, the `already_dialing` and `threshold_reached` values of `kona_node_dial_peer_error` drop and `already_connected` rises. Test logs can be filtered with `RUST_LOG`, and each line is prefixed with `node{id=..}` (see `init_test_tracing`).

**Alternatives**
- The transport is injected as a closure (`GossipTransport::Other`), so production builds contain no memory transport code. The gater lets addresses without an IP through only for that transport.
- Dismissed review findings: sharing `memory_transport()` from kona-gossip, because that would put it back into production code; and making `advertised_port` a `P2PArgs` method.
- Losing gossipsub's subscriptions when duplicates are closed immediately didn't reproduce in 80 crossing dials. Going by the libp2p-gossipsub source it is possible, hence the grace period.

**Potential follow-ups**
- The redial limit only resets after a full period with no dials, and doesn't space out attempts. op-node relies on go-libp2p's per-address backoff instead.
- kona-gossip records counts as gauges; they should be counters. `already_connected` isn't really an error: the network actor shouldn't dial connected peers at all.

Related to #23430. Builds on #23610.

BREAKING CHANGE: `GossipDriverBuilderError`, `Discv5BuilderError` and `NetworkBuilderError` have changed variants (sources added, `WithBehaviourError` removed, new variants), and they no longer derive `Clone`, `PartialEq` or `Eq`. Use `matches!` to compare them. `GaterConfig::default()` now allows unlimited redials.
